title: Security Deposit Account Settlement Rate and the Lease Late-Fee Record
content:
**Q. What sets the settlement rate on a Security Deposit Account settlement payment?**
A. The settlement rate follows two things: the lease's late-fee record in the twenty-four full months before the handling date, and whether recurring autopay is enrolled on the Apartment Home Lease.

- **0.03 (3 percent)** when no late fee was posted on the lease in that time and recurring autopay is enrolled on the lease.
- **0.02 (2 percent)** when exactly one late fee was posted on the lease in that time and recurring autopay is enrolled on the lease.
- **0.01 (1 percent)** in every other case.

**Q. Which records are read?**
A. The late fees posted on the Apartment Home Lease ledger, with their charge dates, counted over the twenty-four full months before the handling date. Also the autopay enrolment recorded on the lease.

**Q. What does the rate do?**
A. The settlement rate is the share of the balance that the settlement allowance takes.

### Truth table

| Late fees on the lease in the 24 months | Autopay enrolled | Settlement rate |
|---|---|---|
| none | yes | 0.03 |
| exactly one | yes | 0.02 |
| two or more | yes | 0.01 |
| none | no | 0.01 |
| exactly one | no | 0.01 |
| two or more | no | 0.01 |

### Boundary cases (hypothetical)

- A late fee posted 25 months before the handling date is outside the twenty-four months. A lease with autopay and only that fee takes 0.03.
- A lease with no late fees but no autopay enrolled takes 0.01.
